RECONCILIATION NOTE: ADR 0013 originally recorded a single 40% threshold on the
mixed workload. That was too coarse — it lets a 4x startup regression pass
(startup is a small share of a mixed run) while failing a benign uniform 45%.
Superseded by the per-workload thresholds below, which reflect that different
workload shapes have genuinely different tolerances. ADR 0013 amended to point

runtimes.$comment: Docker is measured as an intermediate baseline. Without it, a gVisor:native ratio conflates containerisation cost with sandboxing cost, and the two have different remedies.

iterations.$comment: Warmup runs are discarded: page cache and JIT state make the first runs unrepresentative. 25 measured runs is enough for a stable median and IQR on this kind of distribution.

startup.$rationale: Startup is amortised over long jobs but dominates a 10,000-job regression sweep of short simulations. 2x on a ~200ms base is acceptable; more is not.

hdl_parse_large.$rationale: CPU-bound with moderate I/O. Representative of the parser and RTL-index workloads that run on every commit.

lint_tool.$rationale: The typical engineering workload. This is the number that determines whether engineers notice the sandbox.

file_tree_traversal.$rationale: Metadata-heavy syscall stress — the worst case for a userspace kernel. 50% is tolerated because it is a small share of real flow time.

mixed_parse_write.$rationale: End-to-end path: read inputs, parse, write artifacts. Closest proxy for a real job. This is the headline number.

correctness.$rationale: A sandbox that changes results is disqualifying regardless of speed. Compares SHA-256 of normalised stdout plus produced artifacts across all runtimes.

stability.$rationale: If measurements are noisier than 15% CV, the comparison is not meaningful and the run must be repeated on a quieter host. Reporting a ratio from unstable data is worse than reporting nothing.

noUnsupportedSyscalls.$rationale: ADR 0013 flags unimplemented syscalls as a real gVisor failure mode. A workload that fails to run at all is a harder blocker than one that runs slowly.

peakMemoryRatio.$rationale: Sandbox memory overhead multiplies across a large runner fleet and shows up as node-count cost.

outcome.onPass: ADR 0013 confirmed. gVisor remains the default sandbox runtime.
outcome.onFail: ADR 0013 is REOPENED with this evidence attached. Options in order of preference: (1) per-workload runtime selection, (2) Kata as default with gVisor for short jobs, (3) runc + strengthened policy for single-tenant only. Do not silently relax the thresholds.
